sources.note: Nothing. Kenati appears only as 'Kenati family isolate (Ken)' in the abbreviation key (p. 265); no Kenati forms are cited.

sources.citation: Gajdusek, D. Carleton. 1980. Journal of further explorations in the Kuru Region and in the Kukukuku Country, Eastern Highlands of Eastern New Guinea and of a return to West New Guinea: December 25, 1963 to May 4, 1964. Bethesda, MD: NIH (Study of Child Growth and Development and Disease Patterns in Primitive Cultures). Genatei entries 26-29 March 1964, pp. 142-151.
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Ethnographic travel journal (Glottolog 'minimal'): three Genatei villages (Yabuiara, Oropina, Arabunkara), impressionistic remarks that the language 'is clearly closely related to Fore', a 'Fore-Tairora mixture' with 'frequent terminal o', three vocabulary items (sapa 'sweet potato', namo 'house', yabi 'sugar'); mentions Nagra tape recordings of Arubunkara singsings. No linguistic description.

sources.citation: Wurm, Stephen A. 1975. Eastern Central Trans-New Guinea Phylum languages. In S. A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea area languages and language study, vol. 1: Papuan languages and the New Guinea linguistic scene, 461-526. Pacific Linguistics C-38. Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: Nothing on Kenati stress. pp. 466, 472-473: Kenati (Ganati, Aziana) formerly a phylum-level isolate, tentatively a family-level isolate in the East New Guinea Highlands Stock on Lloyd's (1973) lexicostatistics; 'in the absence of structural information on Kenati, this has to remain preliminary'. Sec. 2.7.2.2.5.8 'The Kenati Family', p. 491: 'Very little is known of the structure of Kenati'. The 'Suprasegmentals' paragraphs in this chapter belong to the Wiru (p. 489) and Angan sketches, not Kenati (the earlier nort2920 record's attribution of one to Kenati was wrong).

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3, languoid kena1250 (Hammarström, Forkel, Haspelmath & Bank), and Glottolog reference 311592 (Lloyd 1973) record.
sources.note: Bibliographic only. Glottolog 5.3 lists exactly two references (Gajdusek 1980; Lloyd 1973: 93), the same two as Glottolog 5.1; no phonology, wordlist, sketch or grammar doctype for gat in any provider including silpng. Endangerment note: 'Aziana (gat-gat) = 5* (Developing)' from Ethnologue 2025.

sources.citation: Lloyd, Richard G. 1973. The Angan language family, sec. 2.16 'Neighbouring languages', pp. 93-94 (+ name list p. 106, word-list credits p. 107). In Karl J. Franklin (ed.), The linguistic situation in the Gulf District and adjacent areas, Papua New Guinea. Pacific Linguistics C-26. Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: Nothing. The Glottolog MED. Two paragraphs on Kenati: population 536 'downstream from Wonenara', origin stories (descendants of Baruya and Fore/Gimi), cognate percentages on 170 words (Gimi 19%, Fore 17%, Owena 19%, Awa 12%, Tairora 14%, Waffa 12%; 4-6% with Angan languages), and two roots (taa 'brother', naano 'sister'). Name list p. 106: 'KENATI (Azianan) Ganati (Wurm 1964); Asena or Aziana (Government)'. p. 107 credits the Kenati survey word list to L. Dodd (SIL), unpublished; the list itself is not printed. No phonology, no stress.

Nothing; stub describing Kenati as 'a poorly documented Papuan language' of ~950 speakers in 3 villages of Obura-Wonenara District; classification history (Wurm 1960/1975 isolate branch; Ross 2005 unclassified; Ethnologue 2009 Kainantu); cites only Ethnologue.
